messages:
samir: hey team — customer reports CI failing when fetching our tagged v2 release. build error shows checksum mismatch from goproxy :eyes:
megan: can you paste the exact go.mod + the CI log excerpt?
tyler: here are the relevant bits from their CI (redacted):
```
go: verifying github.com/redwood/inference-go@v2.1.3: checksum mismatch
\	downloaded: h1:abcdef1234567890
\	sum.golang.org: h1:1234567890abcdef
\nprevious fetches for that version succeed locally
```
samir: their go.mod contains:```module github.com/redwood/inference-go

require github.com/redwood/inference-go v2.1.3
```they're using GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org, GOSUMDB=sum.golang.org
jordan: any chance the tag was force-updated after publish? checksum mismatch usually means the content at the tag doesn't match what sum.golang.org saw when it was first recorded. did release engineering retag?
customer-ops: confirming from customer: we pushed a tiny changelog fix and re-tagged the same version to repoint to the new commit because we forgot the changelog entry. they only saw failures after the retag.
megan: ok that's the root cause. if you re-create the tag at a different semver (v2.1.4) and push, that would fix consumer builds. workarounds:
- consumers can run `GOSUMDB=off go get github.com/redwood/inference-go@v2.1.3` but not recommended
- or they can `git fetch --tags` and `GOPROXY=direct go get` to bypass proxy checks

tyler: adding the immediate mitigation we told the customer: advise them to `go clean -modcache` then `GOPROXY=direct go get github.com/redwood/inference-go@v2.1.3` so their CI downloads the current tag from VCS.
jordan: longer term we need a release policy: never move tags. instead publish a new semver patch. also consider signing releases and communicating to downstreams.
support-bot: escalation created: #escalations-4321 — notify release-eng and infra to check whether sum.golang recorded the original content. :shipit:
customer-ops: customer agreed to pin to v2.1.4 when we publish. they also asked for a short note we can paste into their CI explaining the checksum mismatch and recommended fix.
samir: drafting the note now and will include commands and safety warning about disabling sumdb. will follow up once release team cuts v2.1.4. :thumbsup:
